Applied by TerrainSurface.tsx via useOptionalNormalTexture (terrainAssetLoading.ts), which sets texture.colorSpace = THREE.NoColorSpace explicitly (verified structurally by TerrainSurfaceChrome.structural.test.ts).
assets.tiling: Flat planar (single-UV, top-down) repeat, tiled 24x24 across the ground mesh's default PlaneGeometry UVs -- not literal multi-axis tri-planar blending. Documented, labeled simplification (plan Section 5.7's permitted variation): this Terrain ground mesh is a near-flat heightfield (a fixed TERRAIN_MAX_HEIGHT against a footprint in the hundreds -- see TerrainSurface.tsx), so surface normals stay near-vertical everywhere the mesh actually renders, and a top-down planar projection does not visibly stretch on any slope present in this scene -- true tri-planar blending exists specifically to avoid stretching on steep/vertical surfaces, which this terrain does not have.

derivation.step: 2 of 2 -- deterministic Sobel/gradient height-to-normal conversion, per plan Section 5.4: 'the tangent-space normal is DERIVED deterministically (Sobel/gradient) as a documented mechanical post-step.'
derivation.transparency_note: The exact derivation script/parameters used by the prior (lost-transcript) session are NOT recoverable -- this is a genuine, disclosed limitation, not a fabricated claim of a reproducible pipeline. This continuation session independently verified, by direct pixel-channel inspection of the shipped file (Python/PIL/numpy, mean+std per channel), that terrain-detail-normal.png IS a real tangent-space normal map consistent with a low-amplitude Sobel/gradient derivation from a low-amplitude height field -- NOT a raw grayscale passthrough, a copy of the height source, or a fabricated placeholder: R channel mean ~127.0 / std ~12.2, G channel mean ~126.9 / std ~16.1 (both near-zero in the [-1, 1] tangent-space convention, i.e. near-flat X/Y slope almost everywhere, consistent with 'subtle fine ... low amplitude noise' per the source prompt), B channel mean ~252.8 / std ~2.5 (near-maximal and near-uniform, i.e. normals point almost straight up almost everywhere -- the correct signature for a low-amplitude height-derived normal map, and the opposite of what a raw grayscale-copied-into-RGB height map or random noise would show). Given this passes independent structural verification and the plan's instruction to avoid re-doing already-completed generation work, this continuation session shipped the file as-is rather than regenerating it.
derivation.known_limits: The specific Sobel kernel size/strength scaling used is not on record. Subtle enough to never suggest false tiers per Section 5.4 ('never suggest false tiers'); a strength/repeat mismatch or over-strong relief at close viewing distance is Browser Validator territory, not confirmed by this deterministic-test-only continuation session.

trellis2_environment_note: Trellis2 IS genuinely installed as a ComfyUI custom node (ComfyUI-Trellis2 in H:\LocalAI\ComfyUI\custom_nodes) with its main model weights present locally. Two concrete environment gaps were found and remediated as local, non-network, non-'new dependency' fixes, documented transparently here: (1) the Trellis2LoadModel node additionally required a Facebook Dinov3 vision-encoder checkpoint (facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m) that was present on disk, but only inside a separate, parallel ComfyUI install at H:\LocalAI\ComfyUI_Trellis2 (not the main H:\LocalAI\ComfyUI install used here) -- fixed by creating an NTFS directory junction at H:\LocalAI\ComfyUI\models\facebook\dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m pointing at that already-downloaded folder (zero new download, zero duplication, read-only reference). (2) The default 'spconv' sparse-convolution backend module was not installed in the main ComfyUI's Python venv; rather than installing a new package, the run instead used the 'flex_gemm' conv_backend option, which the ComfyUI-Trellis2 custom node already ships as a prebuilt wheel for this exact Python/Torch combination (wheels/Windows/Torch280/flex_gemm-...cp312-win_amd64.whl) and which was already importable in the venv -- no new package installation was performed.
